title: Autoscaler signal voting with grace window for cold-start suppression
creator: Priya Nambiar
postmortem_summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed multiple brief capacity storms where the autoscaler initiated aggressive scale-ups that were not sustained by workload. Traffic showed short high-frequency bursts (sub-30s) caused by client-side retry jitter combined with a metrics aggregation edge-case that amplified a 95th-percentile latency spike. The combined effect produced repeated rapid scale events, causing transient resource churn and higher cost without improved tail latency. This ticket codifies follow-ups and a mitigation design centered on multi-signal voting plus a short grace window to suppress false positive scale-ups during cold-start-prone bursts.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:12 UTC: First sustained 60s spike in p95 latency on shard eu-west-1-serving-12; KEDA scaled from 6->20 replicas within 90s.
2026-03-09 02:14 UTC: Traffic dropped to baseline; HPA quickly scaled down over the next 6 minutes creating churn and warm-pool pressure.
2026-03-09 03:00 UTC: Pager duty resolved immediate customer-facing errors; SRE and runtime on-call started triage.
2026-03-09 09:30 UTC: Initial post-incident sync; hypothesis formed: transient client retries + percentile noise + misaligned aggregation windows.
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC: Root-cause analysis completed; design review planned with platform and runtime teams.
root_cause: Transient sub-minute request bursts combined with 1) a short aggregation window that exaggerated p95 estimates, 2) KEDA trigger expression sensitivity to a single signal (queue depth) and 3) absence of a short consensus/grace mechanism to prevent scale decisions based on single-signal blips.
impact: No long-running customer outages, but increased tail latency for a subset of streaming requests during churn and a 18% spike in GPU reservation cost for the impacted shard during the event window.
decisions: Adopt a lightweight voting mechanism that requires at least 2 of 3 signals (queue_depth, requests_per_second, moving_p95_latency) to exceed thresholds before initiating a scale-up.
Introduce a configurable grace window (default 45s) during which vote consensus must persist before executing scale-up; scale-down remains quicker but rate-limited to avoid flapping.
Add a cold-start score that biases decisions against aggressive scale-up when warm-pool occupancy is below configured thresholds for the pool.
Prioritize runtime-1.20 release for implementing voting logic and expose knobs in Dedicated config and Private deployments via feature flag.
action_items: ENG-990322: Implement voting controller in autoscaler service (owner: Lucas Ortega, due: 2026-03-21) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale/pull/413
ENG-990323: Add 45s default grace window and make configurable via AutoscalerPolicy CRD (owner: Mei Chen, due: 2026-03-18) - design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PI/Grace+Window+Proposal
ENG-990324: Instrument warm-pool occupancy metrics and expose to controller (owner: Darnell Price, due: 2026-03-20) - grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/3abwsz/warm-pool-overview

ENG-990325: Backfill aggregated percentile smoothing (+ longer sliding window fallback) to reduce p95 sensitivity (owner: Akiko Sato, due: 2026-03-25) - RFC: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1aSmoothingRFC

ENG-990326: Create canary rollout plan for runtime-1.20 with step-down and alert hooks (owner: SRE Oncall Rotation, due: 2026-03-28) - runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Autoscaler+Canary
mitigations_deployed: Temporary threshold increase on KEDA queue trigger for eu-west-1-serving-12 to reduce immediate false scale-ups (deployed 2026-03-09 07:00 UTC).
Short-lived metric smoothing (10s->30s) applied to p95 aggregation for affected shards (deployed 2026-03-09 08:45 UTC).
verification_plan: Run chaos-lite testing with synthetic burst generator to validate voting suppresses single-signal blips (owner: QA Eng, due: 2026-03-22).
Compare cost and scale events over two weeks pre/post change using per-shard audit dashboard (owner: Platform Analytics, due: 2026-04-04).
Add golden prompt workload test to ensure latency SLOs remain met under voting policy (owner: Performance Eng, due: 2026-03-26).
open_questions: What is the correct weighting for signals when they disagree (equal-weight vs weighted by signal variance)? Discussion scheduled in architecture sync 2026-03-16.
Should the grace window apply to both hosted and dedicated modes or be tier-specific? Need product guidance from PMs by 2026-03-18.
notes: Design review feedback (2026-03-11): PMs requested a telemetry-first rollout; remove hard-coded thresholds in favor of percentiles relative to baseline.
SRE feedback (2026-03-12): Prefer conservative default (longer grace) and expose a short-circuit for emergency scale-ups.
Cost analysis (2026-03-13): Simulated voting reduces unnecessary scale-ups in 87% of historical blip traces, estimated 10-15% cost savings for low-latency bursts.
